verdict_reason: The candidate's premise that 'no AI has entered the affinage cave' and 'no existing sensor pipeline' is demonstrably false: ML for cheese ripeness is an active field (a 2025 Springer review surveys it), with shipping computer-vision+AI ripeness monitors, deep-learning non-invasive monitoring, MOS/e-nose gas arrays + ANN that discriminate ripening time, TinyML on cheap gas sensors, and ML models of volatile DEVELOPMENT over ripening that already forecast ripening time (the forward-trajectory framing). The technique-agnostic problem and the capability/tool framings are CLOSED. What keeps it merely NARROW rather than fully CLOSED is that no work uses a tiny zero-shot TS foundation model (Reverso-class) for per-wheel edge forecasting of forward gas-signal maturity trajectory; that specific method+deployment is genuinely unoccupied. But the gap is much smaller and more crowded than the candidate claims.

verdict_reason: The candidate's claim — that benchtop/amateur horology 'has no AI diagnostic tooling' and that timegrapher interpretation has 'never been paired with a modern' diagnostic model — is directly contradicted. Timegrapher AI is a live product that ingests the watch's tick acoustics via microphone and explicitly provides AI-powered diagnosis of rate, beat error, amplitude, and escapement irregularities (lock/impulse/unlock phases), i.e. exactly the candidate's 'capture tick acoustics -> flag and locate irregularities -> point the watchmaker at the fault' loop. Several other commercial/DIY mic-based timegrapher apps (Watch Tuner Timegrapher, Calibre, Watch-O-Scope, Tick-Tach) and a peer-reviewed acoustic signature-analysis paper on watch movements provide the same capability. The application (AI/automated diagnosis of mechanical-watch tick traces) already exists, so the gap is closed. The only thing genuinely unused is the SPECIFIC VETime zero-shot vision-enhanced TSAD model/architecture on a beat-timing series, but a directly-equivalent ML/AI diagnostic approach on this exact problem is already deployed, which is the rejection criterion.
